-# Viewstamped Replication for Rust
-
-This is a _work-in-progress_ Rust implementation of the Viewstamped Replication consensus algorithm.
-
-## Getting Started
-
-Run the example:
-
-```console
-cargo run --example example
+# vsr-rs
+
+A Rust implementation of Viewstamped Replication, the consensus protocol
+described in *Viewstamped Replication Revisited* by Liskov and Cowling [1].
+It implements the whole protocol except reconfiguration: normal operation,
+state transfer, view changes, client request deduplication and
+retransmission, and recovery of a replica that crashed and lost its memory,
+with the fixes for the known defects in the paper [3][4].
+
+The library does no I/O and starts no threads. A replica is a state machine
+that its owner steps with incoming messages and idle ticks, and drains for
+outgoing messages afterwards, the way TigerBeetle [5] structures its replica.
+That is what makes it testable in a deterministic simulator, and what lets
+the same code run over sockets, in a simulation, or in a test.
+
+## Getting started
+
+```rust
+use vsr_rs::{Client, Config, Replica, StateMachine};
+
+struct Counter(i64);
+
+impl StateMachine for Counter {
+    type Input = i64;
+    type Output = i64;
+
+    fn apply(&mut self, delta: i64) -> i64 {
+        self.0 += delta;
+        self.0
+    }
+}
+
+let mut config = Config::new();
+for _ in 0..3 {
+    config.add_replica();
+}
+let mut replicas: Vec<_> = (0..3)
+    .map(|id| Replica::new(id, config.clone(), Counter(0)))
+    .collect();
+let mut client = Client::new(0, config);
+
+client.on_request(5);
+loop {
+    // Deliver whatever the client and the replicas want sent. A real
+    // owner would put these on the wire; a test hands them straight over.
+    let mut queue: Vec<_> = client.drain().collect();
+    for replica in &mut replicas {
+        queue.extend(replica.drain_messages());
+        for reply in replica.drain_replies() {
+            println!("request {} -> {}", reply.request_number, reply.result);
+        }
+    }
+    if queue.is_empty() {
+        break;
+    }
+    for (to, message) in queue {
+        replicas[to].on_message(message);
+    }
+}
 ```
 
-To see some debug traces, use `RUST_LOG` environment variable:
+Call `on_idle` on every replica and client at a regular interval: that is
+what drives heartbeats, retransmission, and the view change timer. Persist
+`view_number()` after each step, before sending what the step produced, and
+pass it to `Replica::recover` when a replica comes back from a crash. The
+crate documentation covers the details.
 
-```console
-RUST_LOG=trace cargo run --example example
-```
+Two examples show the library in use:
+
+- [`examples/example.rs`](examples/example.rs) is a version of the loop above.
+- [`examples/kvstore`](examples/kvstore) is a replicated key-value store
+  over TCP that speaks a Redis-like protocol, so you can run three nodes,
+  talk to them with `nc`, and kill the primary.
 
 ## Protocol support
 
-* [x] Normal operation
-* [x] State transfer
-* [x] View changes
-* [x] Client request retransmission and deduplication
-* [x] Failed replica recovery
-* [ ] Reconfiguration
+| Feature | Status |
+|---|---|
+| Normal operation (section 4.1) | done |
+| State transfer (section 5.2), without the truncation defect [4] | done |
+| View changes (section 4.2), with exponential backoff | done |
+| Client table and request retransmission (section 4.1) | done |
+| Recovery (section 4.3), with a persisted view number [3] | done |
+| Reconfiguration (section 7) | not implemented |
 
-## Testing
+Reconfiguration changes the membership of a running cluster. TigerBeetle
+runs the same protocol in production without it, replacing a lost machine
+with a new one that recovers into the same replica id, and the same works
+here. It may come later.
 
-Run the unit tests and the simulator regression tests with:
+## Testing
 
 ```console
 cargo test --workspace
 ```
 
-### Simulator
-
-The `simulator/` crate is a deterministic simulator for the library, modeled
-on TigerBeetle's VOPR. It runs a cluster of replicas and a set of clients in a
-single thread, passes messages through a simulated network that can lose,
-replay, and delay them, and checks a set of properties after every tick.
+runs the cluster tests in [`tests/cluster.rs`](tests/cluster.rs), which
+drive a few replicas by hand and decide which messages get delivered, and
+the simulator's own tests.
 
-The seed determines the whole configuration: cluster size, request rate, idle
-periods, and network fault probabilities are all drawn from the seed's PRNG.
-A run has two phases. In the safety phase, faults are active and the clients
-submit a fixed number of requests. In the liveness phase, faults are disabled
-and every replica must converge to the same fully committed log.
+### Simulator
 
-Run it with a random seed:
+[`simulator/`](simulator) is a deterministic simulator modeled on
+TigerBeetle's VOPR. It runs a cluster and its clients in one thread, passes
+every message through a network that loses, replays, and delays them,
+crashes and restarts replicas, sometimes with their memory wiped, and checks
+a set of safety properties after every tick: committed prefixes agree,
+committed ops survive on enough replicas, every reply matches a committed
+request, no request runs twice. The seed determines the whole configuration,
+from cluster size to fault rates. Once the requests are done, faults stop
+and a random majority of replicas must converge, or the run fails.
 
 ```console
 cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator
 ```
 
-Every run prints its seed. To reproduce a run, pass the seed as an argument:
+Every run prints its seed; pass it back to reproduce the run exactly. A git
+commit hash works as a seed too, which is how CI runs it.
 
 ```console
 cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator -- 10693013600028533629
+cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator -- --lite      # small cluster, fewer requests
+cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator -- --help      # overrides for every fault
 ```
 
-A 40-character git commit hash is also accepted as a seed, which is what CI
-uses, so a CI failure is reproducible from the commit alone:
-
-```console
-cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator -- $(git rev-parse HEAD)
-```
-
-Use `--lite` for a small cluster with fewer requests, and see `--help` for
-overrides such as `--requests-max` and `--packet-loss-probability`. Set
-`RUST_LOG=debug` to see every request and message delivery.
-
-To run the simulator with random seeds on every core for a while, use:
+To run it on every core with random seeds for a while, and get the commands
+to reproduce whatever failed:
 
 ```console
 scripts/simulate --budget 1h
-```
-
-It alternates between lite and full runs, appends one JSON line per run to
-`target/simulate/results.jsonl`, keeps the log of every failed run under
-`target/simulate/logs/`, and prints the commands to reproduce the failures
-at the end. A run that exceeds `--timeout` (default 10 minutes) counts as a
-failure. To see the summary again later, or after an interrupted run:
-
-```console
 scripts/simulate --report
 ```
 
-## References
-
-The implementation of `vsr-rs` is based on the paper [Viewstamped Replication Revisited](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/80846d94-fcd3-40e6-87fb-8d91fe99a5d1) by Liskov and Cowling, which updates the original [Viewstamped Replication: A New Primary Copy Method to Support Highly-Available Distributed Systems](https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/fall11/cos518/papers/viewstamped.pdf) by Oki and Liskov.
-However, the algorithm in the paper has the following known bugs:
-
-* The recovery algorithm described in Section 4.3 can result in the system being in an inconsistent state as reported by Michael et al in Appendix B1 of [Recovering Shared Objects Without Stable Storage](https://drkp.net/papers/recovery-tr17.pdf)
-* The state transfer algorithm described in Section 5.2 can cause data loss as discovered by Jack Vanlightly in https://twitter.com/vanlightly/status/1596190819421413377 and https://twitter.com/vanlightly/status/1596425599026970624.
+Every bug in the history of this repository was found by the simulator and
+is recorded in its commit message with the seed and the commit that
+reproduces it.
 
-`vsr-rs` follows the fixes from Jack Vanlightly's analysis for view changes and state transfer: a replica catching up with a newer view never truncates its log before it has the new view's log to replace the suffix with. For recovery it does what the original Viewstamped Replication did and Michael et al. call for: the view number is persisted, and a recovering replica only rejoins a view at least as recent as the one it persisted.
+## References
 
-The design of `vsr-rs` is inspired by [TigerBeetle](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle), which implements the same protocol in production: a replica is a state machine that its owner steps, with no I/O, clocks, or threads of its own, and the simulator follows TigerBeetle's VOPR, with the seed determining the whole configuration and a liveness core that must converge once faults stop. TigerBeetle's license is in [licenses/tigerbeetle.md](licenses/tigerbeetle.md).
+1. Barbara Liskov and James Cowling. [Viewstamped Replication Revisited](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/80846d94-fcd3-40e6-87fb-8d91fe99a5d1). MIT-CSAIL-TR-2012-021, 2012. The protocol this library implements.
+2. Brian Oki and Barbara Liskov. [Viewstamped Replication: A New Primary Copy Method to Support Highly-Available Distributed Systems](https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/fall11/cos518/papers/viewstamped.pdf). PODC 1988. The original.
+3. Ellis Michael, Dan Ports, Naveen Sharma, and Adriana Szekeres. [Recovering Shared Objects Without Stable Storage](https://drkp.net/papers/recovery-tr17.pdf). Appendix B.1 shows that the recovery protocol of [1] lets two views run at once unless the view number survives a crash.
+4. Jack Vanlightly. [VR Revisited: An Analysis with TLA+](https://jack-vanlightly.com/analyses/2022/12/20/vr-revisited-an-analysis-with-tlaplus). A six part model check of [1]; part 3 shows that truncating the log during state transfer can lose committed data.
+5. [TigerBeetle](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle). A production implementation of Viewstamped Replication whose replica structure and deterministic simulator this library follows. Its license is in [licenses/tigerbeetle.md](licenses/tigerbeetle.md).
+6. Aleksey Charapko. [Reading Group: Viewstamped Replication Revisited](http://charap.co/reading-group-viewstamped-replication-revisited/).
+7. Bruno Bonacci. [Viewstamped Replication Explained](https://blog.brunobonacci.com/2018/07/15/viewstamped-replication-explained/).
